modules.title: Modern HTML5 & Semantic Web Architecture
modules.description: Master document structure, accessibility (WCAG), microdata, and SEO-compliant semantics.

lessons.title: Semantic Elements & DOM Tree Structure
lessons.content:
### Semantic Elements in Modern Web Development
HTML5 semantic elements clearly describe their meaning to both the browser and the developer.
Tags such as `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, `<article>`, and `<footer>` create a structured document outline.

#### Why Semantics Matter:
1. **Accessibility (a11y)**: Screen readers use semantic landmarks to allow assistive tech users to jump directly between page sections.
2. **SEO Optimization**: Search engine crawlers parse your heading hierarchy (`<h1>` through `<h6>`) and landmark tags to deduce page topic relevance.
3. **Maintainability**: Clean semantic markup replaces confusing 'div soup' with readable, self-documenting code.

lessons.title: Forms, Validation & User Input Security
lessons.content:
### Robust Forms & Client-Side Verification
Modern forms must be accessible, responsive, and provide immediate validation feedback without degrading user experience. Always pair `<label for="id">` explicitly with inputs.
lessons.code_example: We'll never share your email with third parties.

questions.question: Which HTML5 element represents the dominant content unit of a page and should only occur once per document?
questions.explanation: <main> specifies the main content of the document. The content inside <main> should be unique to the document and must not occur more than once.

questions.question: How should an accessible form input be linked to its corresponding label?
options: By nesting the label inside the input element
By matching the label's 'for' attribute to the input's 'id'
By setting the input's class name to 'labeled'
Labels and inputs are matched automatically by line order
questions.explanation: The 'for' attribute on a <label> must match the exact 'id' value of the target <input> to establish an accessible programmatic association.

questions.question: Why should you avoid using <div> elements for clickable actions instead of <button>?
options: <div> tags do not receive native keyboard focus (Tab/Enter/Space) and lack button accessibility roles
CSS cannot style <div> elements with hover states
Browsers automatically reject JavaScript click handlers on <div> elements
questions.explanation: <button> comes with built-in keyboard navigation (Tab focus, Enter/Space activation) and correct ARIA roles without manual scripting.

lessons.title: Two-Dimensional Layouts with CSS Grid
lessons.content:
### The Power of CSS Grid
CSS Grid gives you full two-dimensional control over rows and columns simultaneously. Combine `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))` for fluid responsive cards without media queries!

resources.title: CSS Tricks Complete Guide to Grid

questions.question: What CSS property and value combination creates a grid column track that automatically wraps items when space is limited?
questions.explanation: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)) creates dynamic columns that adapt to container width without hardcoded breakpoints.

questions.question: Which Flexbox property aligns items along the cross axis?
questions.explanation: 'align-items' aligns flex items along the cross axis, whereas 'justify-content' aligns items along the main axis.

lessons.title: Promises and Concurrent API Orchestration
lessons.content:
### Non-Blocking Asynchronous JavaScript
Mastering `Promise.allSettled()`, `async/await`, and handling network errors gracefully ensures your web app remains responsive under unstable connections.

questions.question: Where do resolved Promise callbacks get queued in the JavaScript Event Loop?
questions.explanation: Resolved Promises are placed in the Microtask queue, which is drained completely before the next Macrotask (e.g., setTimeout) is executed.

### Custom Hook Encapsulation
Extract reusable business and data fetching logic into self-contained React hooks to separate concerns cleanly between UI presentation and state management.

questions.question: When does the cleanup function returned by useEffect execute?
options: Only when the browser window closes
Before re-running the effect on dependency change and when unmounting
questions.explanation: Effect cleanup runs before re-invoking the effect when dependencies change, and during component unmount to prevent memory leaks.

lessons.title: Matrix Operations & Feature Scaling
lessons.content:
### Vectorized Math with NumPy
Feature scaling ensures gradient descent converges rapidly. Standardize features to mean=0 and variance=1 before feeding into linear models.

questions.question: Why is feature scaling crucial for gradient-based optimization algorithms?
options: It prevents gradient descent from oscillating wildly across asymmetric cost surfaces
It turns continuous data into categorical integers
It guarantees 100% accuracy on the test set
It deletes missing values from the dataset
questions.explanation: When features have vastly different scales, the loss surface resembles an elongated ellipse, causing gradient descent to bounce inefficiently. Scaling creates symmetric contours.

lessons.content:
### Grounding Generative Models
RAG augments LLMs with private, verified knowledge bases. We vectorize documents into dense semantic embeddings and perform cosine similarity search via vector indexes.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over fine-tuning for factual query answering?
options: RAG provides real-time verifiable document grounding without expensive retraining and reduces hallucinations
RAG makes the model run without an internet connection
RAG permanently rewrites the transformer weights
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves factual chunks at query time, passing them in-context so the model can cite exact sources without model retraining.
